findings.description: `request_ai()` now reserves a scheduled follow-up's original due day as its reply day, even when that day is less than 90 days away. If the asynchronous response arrives after that day is sealed, admission rejects it; the pending request is then removed at the due day even without a reply, so the follow-up cannot appear.
findings.title: AI follow-ups vanish at high speed

citations.citation: project-keynes-narrative-events

evidence.explanation: The narrative skill calls for asynchronous AI generation and scheduled follow-up events. The new scheduling branch shortens the reply window to the remaining time before the original due day; the native consumer erases unanswered requests on that day, while admission requires the response to match the now-sealed day.

findings.description: `capture()` writes multiple pending AI requests under a new `pending_ai_requests` key but leaves `version` at 1. A build that reads only the single `pending_ai_request` slot silently drops the extra requests when it loads such a save.
findings.title: Old builds lose queued AI requests

citations.citation: Keynes: new continuation state is versioned, validated and installed atomically
out["version"] = 1;

evidence.explanation: The checkpoint adds a continuation list (`pending_ai_requests`) that affects later days, and the `version` literal stays at 1. The new validator accepts the key, but readers of the old format never check for it, so they lose the extra requests without an error.

findings.description: `poll_runtime_commit` now publishes boundary results that the changed GDScript consumes, but the checked-in Android, macOS and Web libraries were restored to their baseline versions. Running the game with those libraries leaves the new command-settlement and quote-ready paths without the native results they require; the runtime CI build only replaces the Linux library.
findings.title: Platform builds run outdated native logic

findings.description: The military seal test used to assert a fixed effective day of `settled_day + 1` but now computes `expected` from the receipt's own committed and frozen fields and asserts `admitted == expected`. Because the expectation is derived from the output it checks, a shift of the admission boundary by one day can still pass.
findings.title: Date check now follows the system output

findings.description: `checkpoint_error` only checks that `version` is an integer. It never compares it with the value `capture()` writes (1), and `decode_checkpoint` does not branch on it either. So a narrative archive with an unsupported version passes validation and is decoded with the current field layout instead of being rejected.
findings.title: Narrative saves from a newer format load as if they were the current one

evidence.explanation: The validator only type-checks `version`. `capture` writes `version = 1`, and `configure` decodes right after validation with no version check.

findings.description: When the worker shuts down, it now clears `_economy_boundary_requests`, `_colonization_read_results` and `_colonization_quotes_ready`. It does this without publishing a result or a readiness signal for quote reads it had already accepted and answered with `pending`. The planner panel retries a stored read only from `_on_colonization_quotes_ready`, so if a restart or fault drops an in-flight quote read, the "结算中" (settling) status stays up until the player reopens or refreshes the panel.
findings.title: Colonization panel can stay stuck on "settling" after a runtime stop

evidence.explanation: Quote reads return `pending`/`busy` and are queued for the worker. The panel keeps a retry callable that only the readiness signal triggers. Worker shutdown clears the queue and the readiness flag without notifying anyone, so the stored callables never run.
